e: Originally arising through erroneous interpretations of Middle Welsh terms; the scribal error mabynnogyon being construed as the plural for Welsh mabinogi, which is already plural. See citation 1887 below. More information at Mabinogion.
q: I recollect a Mabinogi, or mythological tale, respecting this piece of water, which runs thus: - In ancient times a door in a rock near tins lake was found open upon a certain day every year.

So greatly do these Mabinogion differ in character, that they may be considered as forming two distinct classes; one of which generally celebrates heroes of the Arthurian cycle, while the other refers to persons and events of an earlier period, and it not difficult to assign each tale to one or other of these two classes[.]

The Welsh Mabinogis of 'Pereduh," which relates the same incidents as these two poems, and in which the hero is certainly identical, knows no Grail, only a Dish with a Bleeding Head, and the Bleeding Lance, probably the original talisman of the story.
